The rename to Codwen in 1.4.0 is byte-neutral by construction - 34 insertions for 34 deletions of same-length strings - and it is what tipped the class over: the same bytes compressed to six more bytes than the ceiling. Raised to the next whole KiB rather than by the script's 5 percent, which would have cost 26 KB of headroom for a 6-byte overrun. 2026-11-25: targetDebugBytes 15.00 -> 20.00 GB, measured 18.34 GB (incremental 4.80, deps 9.99, build 1.29, examples 1.40). That is the live working set of a full verify on a fourteen-crate workspace - clippy --all-targets, forty-nine test binaries and the prove examples - not abandoned output: -Prune freed 0 bytes because the version sweep bumped Cargo.lock in the same hour, which makes every incremental unit current by this script's own cutoff rule. Raising it once, with the measurement written down, is the honest alternative to deleting build output that the next verify would rebuild. 2026-11-25, later the same day: targetDebugBytes 20.00 -> 24.00 GB, measured 22.09 GB (incremental 7.68, deps 10.79, build 1.29, examples 1.46) straight after back-to-back full verifies of one fourteen-crate workspace. The growth is one cycle of live units rather than accumulation: the two largest are the desktop library's incremental units at 1.39 GB and 0.80 GB, written minutes earlier by this gate's own clippy --all-targets and its forty-nine test binaries, and -Prune frees 0 bytes by the cutoff rule it documents because nothing there is stale. A ceiling that verifying the workspace once cannot stay under is measuring the verification rather than the waste, so it is raised to the next whole GiB above the measurement with the figures recorded here. 2026-11-25, later the same day: shipped 533.0 -> 536.0 KB, measured 535.3 KB by the devcloud run of the verify lane ts on commit e7dd3b6, for the agent collaboration page (S26-13): a lazily imported screen with three sections - agents present, conversations, work in progress - polling while it is visible, a Motion enter and exit on every row, four icons and the strings in both locales.
